707-320.fun_fact: The 707 is widely credited with launching the Jet Age and transforming commercial aviation when it entered service in 1958.

727-200.fun_fact: The 727-200 was the world's best-selling commercial jet at the time of its retirement, with over 1,830 built.

737-200.fun_fact: The 737-200 was the original Classic variant of the world's most successful commercial jetliner family.

737-300.fun_fact: The 737-300 introduced high-bypass CFM56 turbofan engines, dramatically improving fuel efficiency over earlier 737 variants.

737-400.fun_fact: The 737-400 was the largest Classic 737, filling the gap between medium and longer-haul narrow-body operations.

737-500.fun_fact: The 737-500 was designed as a direct replacement for the 737-200, offering identical capacity with far more efficient CFM56 engines.

737-600.fun_fact: The 737-600 is the smallest member of the Next Generation family and sold in by far the fewest numbers of any NG variant.

737-700.fun_fact: The 737-700 is the basis for the US Navy and Air Force C-40 Clipper VIP and logistics transport aircraft.

737-800.fun_fact: The 737-800 is the most-produced NG variant, with over 4,900 delivered — a cornerstone of short-haul aviation worldwide.

737-900.fun_fact: Alaska Airlines was the sole launch customer for the 737-900, the longest member of the original NG family.

747-100.fun_fact: Pan Am Flight 1 on January 22, 1970 was the inaugural 747 service, launching the Jumbo Jet era of mass air travel.

747-200.fun_fact: The 747-200 introduced more powerful engines and greater range than the -100, and became the definitive intercontinental workhorse of the 1970s.

747-300.fun_fact: The 747-300 replaced the upper-deck staircase with a full cabin section, boosting passenger capacity and reducing the crew from three to two.

747-400.fun_fact: The 747-400 was the first large commercial aircraft with a two-crew glass cockpit, eliminating the traditional flight engineer position.

757-200.fun_fact: The 757-200 had an exceptional climb rate for a narrow-body and pioneered ETOPS-approved transatlantic operations for twin-engine jets.

757-300.fun_fact: The 757-300 is the longest narrow-body airliner Boeing ever built, yet only 55 were produced due to limited market demand.

767-200.fun_fact: The 767-200 was the first wide-body airliner to receive ETOPS-120 approval, enabling twin-engine transatlantic service.

767-300.fun_fact: The 767-300 remains widely used as a freighter, with hundreds of passenger aircraft converted for cargo operations.

767-400.fun_fact: The 767-400ER is the largest and longest-range 767 variant, yet only 38 were ever ordered, making it a commercial rarity.

777-200.fun_fact: The 777 was the first commercial aircraft designed entirely using 3D CAD software, a milestone in aerospace engineering.

777-300.fun_fact: At 73.9 metres, the 777-300 is the longest twinjet airliner ever to enter production.

A300B4.fun_fact: The A300 was the world's first twin-engine wide-body airliner and the first aircraft to bear the Airbus name.

A310.fun_fact: The A310 was the first commercial airliner equipped with a fully computerised two-crew EFIS glass cockpit.

A318.fun_fact: British Airways flew the A318 on a unique all-business-class transatlantic service to New York using the short-runway London City Airport.

A319.fun_fact: The A319CJ corporate jet variant is flown by heads of state worldwide, offering transcontinental range in a narrow-body airframe.

A320.fun_fact: The A320 was the first commercial airliner to use full fly-by-wire controls with digital flight envelope protection, setting a new standard for safety.

A321.fun_fact: The forthcoming A321XLR will fly over 8,700 km non-stop, enabling single-aisle transatlantic routes between Europe and the US East Coast.

A330-200.fun_fact: The A330-200 doubles as a multi-role tanker-transport in its MRTT military version, serving the air forces of more than ten nations.

A330-300.fun_fact: The A330-300 shares 95% commonality with the four-engine A340-300, allowing airlines to cross-qualify flight crews on both types.

A340-200.fun_fact: At introduction the A340-200 held the record for the world's longest non-stop commercial flight, operated by Singapore Airlines between Singapore and New York.

A340-300.fun_fact: The A340-300 was favoured on routes restricted from ETOPS, where its four engines gave a regulatory advantage over twin-engine aircraft.

A340-500.fun_fact: Singapore Airlines operated the A340-500 on the world's longest-ever non-stop commercial flights — nearly 19 hours between Singapore and Newark.

A340-600.fun_fact: At 75.36 m the A340-600 was the world's longest commercial airliner until the Boeing 747-8 Intercontinental surpassed it in 2011.

A380.fun_fact: The A380 is the world's largest passenger airliner, featuring a full-length double deck with two cabin aisles on every level.

ATR-42.fun_fact: The ATR 42 was the launch product of the ATR consortium and inspired an entire generation of modern regional turboprops.

ATR-72.role: Short to medium-range regional passenger transport
ATR-72.fun_fact: The ATR 72 is the world's best-selling turboprop airliner and is the primary link between remote island communities across Southeast Asia.

An-12.fun_fact: The An-12 is the Soviet equivalent of the C-130 Hercules and served in over 30 countries throughout the Cold War.

BAE 146-200.fun_fact: The BAe 146 is exceptionally quiet for a jet, enabling operations at noise-restricted airports like London City that ban other jets.

BAE 146-300.fun_fact: The BAe 146-300 serves as the Statesman VIP transport for the Royal Air Force and the CC-142 in the Canadian Forces.

BAE-125.fun_fact: The BAe 125 has been in continuous production for over six decades, making it one of the longest-running business jet designs in history.

Beechcraft 1900.fun_fact: The Beechcraft 1900D is rare among aircraft its size for having a stand-up cabin, providing unusual comfort for commuter passengers.

Boeing 717.fun_fact: The Boeing 717 traces its lineage directly to the DC-9 of 1965, representing one of aviation's longest unbroken design lineages.

C-130.role: Tactical military cargo and personnel transport
C-130.fun_fact: The C-130 Hercules has been in continuous production for over 65 years, making it the longest-produced military aircraft in history.

C-47.engines: 2x Pratt & Whitney R-1830-90C Twin Wasp radial
C-47.fun_fact: On D-Day, C-47s dropped over 13,000 paratroopers of the 82nd and 101st Airborne Divisions behind enemy lines in Normandy.

CRJ-200.fun_fact: Over 1,000 CRJ200s were produced, making it the backbone of North American regional aviation throughout the 2000s.

CRJ-700.role: Short to medium-range regional passenger transport
CRJ-700.fun_fact: The CRJ700 was the first regional jet to offer reclining seats and overhead bins comparable to those on mainline aircraft.

CRJ-900.role: Short to medium-range regional passenger transport
CRJ-900.fun_fact: The CRJ900 introduced winglets that improved fuel efficiency and extended range compared to earlier CRJ variants.

Cessna 172.fun_fact: The Cessna 172 is the most produced aircraft in history, with over 44,000 built since 1956.

Cessna 208.role: Regional cargo and passenger feeder service
Cessna 208.fun_fact: The Cessna 208 Caravan operates on floats, skis, and wheels, making it one of the most versatile utility aircraft ever built.

Cessna 525.fun_fact: The CJ1 was the first FAA-certified business jet in its class approved for single-pilot operation, democratising jet ownership.

Cessna 560.fun_fact: The Citation V became a charter-operator favourite because it can use short runways while still delivering respectable jet performance.

Challenger 600.fun_fact: The Challenger 600 was the first business jet to offer a true wide-body fuselage cross-section, providing stand-up cabin comfort.

DC-10.fun_fact: The DC-10 features a distinctive third engine mounted at the base of the vertical tail, a layout shared with its rival the Lockheed L-1011 TriStar.

DC-3.engines: 2x Pratt & Whitney R-1830-92 Twin Wasp radial
DC-3.fun_fact: Remarkably, some Douglas DC-3s built in the 1930s remain in active commercial service, making them among the oldest airliners still flying passengers.

DC-6.engines: 4x Pratt & Whitney R-2800-CB17 Double Wasp radial
DC-6.fun_fact: The DC-6B was used as the US Presidential aircraft before dedicated Air Force One jets, carrying President Eisenhower on state visits.

DC-8.fun_fact: In 1961 a DC-8 became the first commercial jet to intentionally exceed the speed of sound, reaching Mach 1.012 during a controlled test dive.

DC-9-30.fun_fact: The DC-9-30 is the direct ancestor of the MD-80, MD-90, and Boeing 717, forming one of commercial aviation's most enduring design lineages.

DH-82.fun_fact: Over 8,000 Tiger Moths were built, and the type trained the vast majority of Commonwealth pilots who flew in World War II.

DHC-1.engines: 1x de Havilland Gipsy Major 10 Mk.2 piston
DHC-1.fun_fact: King Charles III received his first fixed-wing flying training in a Chipmunk at Cambridge University in 1968.

DHC-6.full_name: de Havilland Canada DHC-6 Twin Otter
DHC-6.role: STOL regional passenger and cargo transport
DHC-6.fun_fact: The Twin Otter is the world's most widely used seaplane, providing the essential air links between atolls in the Maldives.

DHC-8-100.fun_fact: The DHC-8-100 was built with STOL capability to serve remote Canadian communities on short, unimproved airstrips.

DHC-8-300.role: Short to medium-range regional passenger transport
DHC-8-300.fun_fact: The DHC-8-300 stretched the original Dash 8 fuselage by 3.4 metres, significantly boosting capacity for regional operators.

DR-400.fun_fact: The DR 400 is the most popular light aircraft in France, a staple of French aero clubs and flying schools for over 50 years.

Dornier 328.fun_fact: The Dornier 328 was later offered as the 328JET with turbofan engines, becoming one of the fastest regional aircraft in its size class.

E-170.role: Short to medium-range regional passenger transport
E-170.fun_fact: The E170 introduced a 2-2 seating layout to regional jets, guaranteeing every passenger either an aisle or a window seat.

E-190.role: Short to medium-range regional passenger transport
E-190.fun_fact: JetBlue built its entire hub-and-spoke model around the E190, becoming the aircraft's launch and largest customer.

E-195.fun_fact: The E195 is the largest E-Jet variant and offers near-mainline cabin width in one of the most fuel-efficient aircraft of its era.

EMB-120.fun_fact: The EMB 120 Brasilia was the world's fastest turboprop commuter aircraft when introduced and launched Embraer onto the international stage.

ERJ 135.fun_fact: The ERJ 135 was derived from the ERJ 145 with a shortened fuselage, sharing 95% parts commonality with its larger sibling.

ERJ 145.role: Short to medium-range regional passenger transport
ERJ 145.fun_fact: The ERJ 145 was the aircraft that transformed Embraer from a regional manufacturer into a major global commercial aviation player.

Embraer Legacy 600.fun_fact: The Legacy 600 is an executive conversion of the ERJ 145 regional jet, featuring long-range tanks and a luxurious cabin interior.

Eurofighter Typhoon.fun_fact: The Typhoon is deliberately designed to be aerodynamically unstable, a feature that maximises agility in combat but requires fly-by-wire computers to keep it airborne.

F-16A/B.fun_fact: The F-16A/B was the first production fighter to fly with a relaxed static stability fly-by-wire system, making it exceptionally manoeuvrable.

F/A-18.fun_fact: The F/A-18 was the first aircraft designed simultaneously as both a fighter and an attack platform, earning the unique F/A dual designation.

Falcon 2000.fun_fact: The Falcon 2000 brought a wide-body cross-section to Dassault's business jet line, offering airline-like cabin comfort in a mid-range jet.

Falcon 900.fun_fact: The Falcon 900's three-engine layout and long range enabled it to reach virtually any two cities in the world with a single stop.

Fokker 100.fun_fact: The Fokker 100 was the last commercial aircraft produced by Fokker before the company went bankrupt in 1996.

Fokker 50.role: Short to medium-range regional passenger transport
Fokker 50.fun_fact: The Fokker 50 is a modernised successor to the iconic Fokker F27 Friendship, one of the most successful turboprops ever built.

Fokker 70.role: Short to medium-range regional passenger transport
Fokker 70.fun_fact: The Fokker 70 was essentially a shortened Fokker 100, developed rapidly in less than four years to meet demand for smaller-capacity jets.

Global Express.fun_fact: When it entered service in 1998, the Global Express was the first business jet capable of flying non-stop between any two cities on Earth.

Gulfstream IV.fun_fact: The Gulfstream IV introduced a new supercritical wing that allowed significantly higher cruise speeds than any previous Gulfstream model.

Gulfstream V.fun_fact: The Gulfstream V was the first business jet certified for transatlantic ETOPS-180 operation, transforming ultra-long-range private aviation.

Hawk T1.role: Advanced military flight training and light attack
Hawk T1.fun_fact: The Hawk T1 is flown by the RAF Red Arrows, making it one of the most instantly recognisable aircraft in the world.

Il-76.role: Heavy strategic airlift and cargo transport
Il-76.fun_fact: The Il-76 can operate from unpaved runways and has a pressurised rear ramp that enables cargo loading even at altitude.

L-1011.fun_fact: The L-1011 was the first commercial aircraft with a fully automated landing system capable of Category IIIC zero-visibility landings.

MD-11.fun_fact: The MD-11 is now used almost exclusively as a freighter; it was among the last commercial trijets ever built.

MD-80.fun_fact: American Airlines operated over 300 MD-80s at peak, the largest fleet of this type in the world.

MD-87.fun_fact: The MD-87 was the shortest MD-80 variant and was particularly popular with Scandinavian carriers serving smaller, thinner routes.

MD-90.fun_fact: The MD-90's IAE V2500 turbofan engines made it dramatically quieter than the MD-80, helping it meet strict airport noise regulations.

Metroliner.fun_fact: The Metroliner's unusually narrow fuselage earned it the nickname 'the flying pencil' or 'the flying tube' among its frequent flyers.

Model B200.fun_fact: The King Air B200 is the world's best-selling turboprop aircraft, with over 3,000 delivered since 1974.

PA-28.fun_fact: The PA-28 Cherokee was designed by John Thorp and broke with traditional Piper high-wing designs by adopting a low-wing configuration.

SR-20.fun_fact: The SR20 was the first FAA-certified aircraft to come with a whole-aircraft parachute system (CAPS) as standard equipment.

Saab 2000.role: Short to medium-range regional passenger transport
Saab 2000.fun_fact: The Saab 2000 is one of the fastest turboprop airliners ever built, cruising at jet-like speeds to compete directly with regional jets.

Saab 340.fun_fact: The Saab 340 was originally co-developed with Fairchild Aircraft before Saab bought out Fairchild's entire share in 1985.

Spitfire.fun_fact: The Spitfire's distinctive elliptical wing was designed by R.J. Mitchell to allow the thinnest possible section, maximising speed and manoeuvrability.

Tornado.fun_fact: The Tornado's variable-sweep wings can be set from 25° for takeoff to 67° for high-speed flight, optimising performance across all regimes.

Tu-134.fun_fact: The Tu-134 featured a distinctive glazed nose section housing a navigator, a design inherited from Soviet bomber traditions.

Tu-154.fun_fact: The Tu-154 was the Soviet Union's dominant narrow-body and served as the workhorse of Aeroflot operations for over 40 years.

Yak-42.fun_fact: The Yak-42 was the first Soviet airliner designed specifically to replace the Tu-134 on medium-range domestic Soviet routes.

A400M Atlas.country: EU (France / Germany / UK / Spain / Belgium / Luxembourg / Turkey)
A400M Atlas.fun_fact: The A400M can carry a main battle tank and also serve as an aerial refuelling tanker using under-wing fuel pods — a unique dual capability.

AG-600 Kunlong.role: Maritime patrol, search and rescue, and aerial firefighting
AG-600 Kunlong.fun_fact: The AG-600 is the world's largest amphibious aircraft and can scoop 12 tonnes of water in just 20 seconds during firefighting runs.

An-124 Ruslan.fun_fact: The An-124 can carry outsized payloads impossible for any other aircraft, including space rockets, power plant generators, and even disassembled smaller aircraft.

An-22 Antei.fun_fact: The An-22 Antei was the world's largest aircraft for 12 years after its debut and remains the largest turboprop-powered aircraft ever built.

An-225 Mriya.role: Outsized cargo and space vehicle transport
An-225 Mriya.fun_fact: The An-225 Mriya was the world's largest and heaviest aircraft ever built, holding 240 world records before being destroyed during Russia's invasion of Ukraine in February 2022.

An-72 Coaler.fun_fact: The An-72's engines are mounted above the wings to direct jet exhaust over the upper wing surface, dramatically increasing lift for exceptional STOL performance.

B-1B Lancer.role: Long-range strategic conventional and nuclear bombing
B-1B Lancer.fun_fact: The B-1B Lancer has variable-sweep wings adjustable from 15° to 67.5° and can carry more conventional weapons than any other aircraft in the US Air Force inventory.

B-2 Spirit.role: Strategic nuclear and conventional stealth bombing
B-2 Spirit.fun_fact: Each B-2 Spirit costs over $2.1 billion including development costs, making it the most expensive military aircraft ever built.

B-21 Raider.role: Strategic nuclear and conventional stealth bombing
B-21 Raider.fun_fact: The B-21 Raider is the first new American bomber in 34 years and is designed from the outset to be capable of fully uncrewed autonomous operations.

B-52 Stratofortress.role: Long-range strategic nuclear and conventional bombing
B-52 Stratofortress.fun_fact: The B-52H has been in continuous service since 1955 and is expected to fly until at least 2050 — nearly a century of service for a single aircraft type.

Be-200 Altair.role: Aerial firefighting, maritime patrol, and search and rescue
Be-200 Altair.fun_fact: The Be-200 is the world's only purpose-built jet-powered aerial firefighting aircraft and can scoop 12 tonnes of water in just 14 seconds.

C-1 Trader.fun_fact: The C-1 Trader was derived from the S-2 Tracker anti-submarine aircraft and served as the US Navy's primary carrier onboard delivery aircraft for over 30 years.

C-130 Hercules.role: Tactical military cargo, paratroop, and airdrop transport
C-130 Hercules.fun_fact: The C-130 Hercules family has been in continuous production for over 65 years and remains the only military aircraft ever to land on an aircraft carrier without arresting gear.

C-17 Globemaster.fun_fact: The C-17 can deliver cargo to short, austere runways and then reverse thrust to back up without turning around — a unique ground-manoeuvring capability.

C-2 Greyhound.fun_fact: The C-2 Greyhound is being replaced by the CMV-22B Osprey tiltrotor, which will give the US Navy far greater range for carrier onboard delivery missions.

C-390 Millennium.role: Tactical military cargo transport and aerial refuelling
C-390 Millennium.fun_fact: The KC-390 is the largest aircraft ever designed and built entirely in Brazil, and can carry armoured vehicles, helicopters, or act as a tanker in the same mission.

C-5 Galaxy.fun_fact: The C-5 Galaxy can simultaneously transport two M1 Abrams battle tanks, making it the largest aircraft in the US Air Force inventory.

CL-415 SuperScooper.fun_fact: The CL-415 can scoop 6,137 litres of water in 12 seconds while skimming across a lake at 150 km/h, then drop it within minutes.

E-2 Hawkeye.role: Carrier-based airborne early warning and battle management
E-2 Hawkeye.fun_fact: The E-2 Hawkeye is the only turboprop-powered aircraft currently operating from US Navy supercarriers and serves as the carrier air wing's airborne command post.

E-7 Wedgetail.role: Airborne early warning, battle management, and communications
E-7 Wedgetail.fun_fact: The E-7's dorsal-mounted MESA radar can simultaneously track hundreds of airborne and surface targets across a 360-degree field of view.

EMB-314 Super Tucano.role: Counter-insurgency, light attack, and advanced flight training
EMB-314 Super Tucano.fun_fact: The Super Tucano beat jet aircraft competitors to win the US Air Force's Afghan Air Force light air support programme, becoming the first propeller aircraft selected in such a competition in decades.

H-6.role: Strategic bombing and cruise missile carrier
operators: People's Liberation Army Naval Air Force
H-6.fun_fact: The H-6K is a modern Chinese derivative of the 1950s Soviet Tu-16 Badger and can carry six CJ-20 cruise missiles capable of striking US bases across the Western Pacific.

Il-76 Candid.role: Strategic airlift and commercial outsized cargo transport
Il-76 Candid.fun_fact: The Il-76 Candid has a unique pressurised cargo hold with an integral loading ramp, enabling operations from short, unpaved airstrips in the most remote locations on Earth.

KC-135 Stratotanker.role: Strategic aerial refuelling and secondary cargo transport
KC-135 Stratotanker.fun_fact: The KC-135 can offload over 68,000 kg of fuel and has refuelled every major US combat aircraft since the Vietnam War — a 65-year refuelling legacy.

P-3 Orion.fun_fact: The P-3 Orion was designed using the Lockheed Electra commercial turboprop as its structural basis, dramatically cutting development cost and time.

SR-71 Blackbird.engines: 2x Pratt & Whitney J58-1 continuous-bleed afterburning turbojet
SR-71 Blackbird.fun_fact: The SR-71 could outrun surface-to-air missiles simply by accelerating — no SR-71 was ever shot down, and over 4,000 missiles were fired at it without success.

Tu-160 Blackjack.fun_fact: The Tu-160 Blackjack is the world's largest combat aircraft and the heaviest supersonic aircraft ever built; its crews affectionately call it the 'White Swan'.

Tu-22M Backfire.role: Long-range strategic and anti-ship strike bombing
Tu-22M Backfire.fun_fact: NATO planners considered the Tu-22M Backfire one of the most dangerous Cold War threats because its maritime strike role could sever transatlantic shipping lanes in a conflict.

Tu-95 Bear.role: Long-range strategic nuclear bomber and cruise missile carrier
Tu-95 Bear.fun_fact: The Tu-95 Bear's contra-rotating turboprop engines make it the loudest aircraft ever recorded — loud enough to be detected by sonar systems aboard submerged submarines.

U-2 Dragon Lady.fun_fact: U-2 pilots wear full pressure suits identical to those of astronauts, and the aircraft is so difficult to land that a chase car and second pilot guide it down on every single landing.

US-2 ShinMaywa.role: Maritime search and rescue and amphibious patrol
US-2 ShinMaywa.fun_fact: The US-2 can land on and take off from waves up to 3 metres high, enabling life-saving rescues in severe open-ocean conditions.

V-22 Osprey.role: Multi-mission tactical transport and special operations
V-22 Osprey.fun_fact: The V-22 Osprey takes off and lands like a helicopter but cruises like a turboprop, combining both capabilities through its revolutionary proprotor nacelles that tilt 90 degrees.

XB-70 Valkyrie.fun_fact: The XB-70 used 'compression lift', riding its own shockwave at Mach 3 to generate free aerodynamic lift — a revolutionary concept never replicated in any production aircraft.

A-10 Thunderbolt.role: Close air support and anti-armour ground attack
A-10 Thunderbolt.fun_fact: The A-10 was essentially built around its GAU-8 Avenger 30mm cannon — so powerful that firing it actually slows the aircraft down.

AV-8B Harrier.role: Short take-off and vertical landing close air support and ground attack
AV-8B Harrier.fun_fact: The Harrier can hover in mid-air and fly backwards using its vectored-thrust nozzles, giving it operational flexibility from tiny ships and improvised jungle clearings.

Avro Vulcan.fun_fact: In 1982 an Avro Vulcan flew the world's longest bombing mission — a 13,000 km round trip to the Falkland Islands and back — known as Operation Black Buck.

Dassault Rafale.role: Air superiority, ground attack, nuclear strike, and reconnaissance
Dassault Rafale.fun_fact: The Rafale went 30 years without a single export customer before Egypt broke the drought in 2015 — it has since become one of the most sought-after fighters on the market.

F-117 Nighthawk.fun_fact: The F-117's faceted stealth design was based on mathematical papers by Soviet physicist Pyotr Ufimtsev — ironically published openly and unrecognised as militarily significant in the USSR.

F-14 Tomcat.role: Carrier-based fleet air defence and air superiority
operators: Islamic Republic of Iran Air Force
F-14 Tomcat.fun_fact: The F-14's AWG-9 radar and AIM-54 Phoenix missiles could track 24 targets and engage six simultaneously at ranges of over 160 km — a capability unmatched for decades.

F-15 Eagle.fun_fact: The F-15 Eagle has a perfect air combat record with over 104 confirmed aerial victories and zero losses in dogfights — unmatched by any other fighter in history.

F-16 Fighting Falcon.role: Air superiority, ground attack, and suppression of enemy air defences
F-16 Fighting Falcon.fun_fact: With over 4,600 built for 25 nations, the F-16 Fighting Falcon is the most produced Western jet fighter aircraft in history.

F-22 Raptor.role: Stealth air superiority, suppression of enemy air defences, and precision ground attack
F-22 Raptor.fun_fact: The F-22 can supercruise at Mach 1.82 without using its afterburner, making it virtually impossible for older-generation fighters to intercept or escape.

F-35 Lightning II.role: Stealth air superiority, ground attack, and electronic warfare
F-35 Lightning II.fun_fact: The F-35's helmet-mounted display lets pilots effectively see through the aircraft's own floor and fuselage walls by projecting live sensor feeds from cameras embedded around the airframe.

F-4 Phantom.role: Air superiority, ground attack, and strategic reconnaissance
F-4 Phantom.fun_fact: The F-4 Phantom II is the only aircraft ever to simultaneously serve as the premier frontline fighter for the US Navy, Marine Corps, and Air Force at the same time.

F/A-18 Hornet.role: Carrier-based air superiority and precision strike
F/A-18 Hornet.fun_fact: The F/A-18 was the first aircraft designed simultaneously for both fighter and attack roles, earning the dual F/A designation that was unprecedented in US military aviation.

J-10 Vigorous Dragon.role: Air superiority and precision ground attack
J-10 Vigorous Dragon.fun_fact: The J-10 was China's first fully indigenous fourth-generation multirole fighter, ending decades of near-total dependence on Soviet and Russian combat aircraft designs.

J-20 Mighty Dragon.role: Stealth air superiority, strategic interception, and precision strike
J-20 Mighty Dragon.fun_fact: The J-20 made China only the second country in the world to field an operational indigenous fifth-generation stealth fighter, after the United States.

J-50.role: Carrier-based stealth air superiority and precision strike
operators: People's Liberation Army Naval Air Force
J-50.fun_fact: The J-50's tailless cranked-kite delta wing design makes it China's first purpose-built carrier stealth fighter, representing a generational leap in Chinese naval aviation capability.

JAS-39 Gripen.role: Air superiority, ground attack, and maritime strike
JAS-39 Gripen.fun_fact: The Gripen is designed to operate from ordinary public roads, and a ground crew of just five technicians can refuel and rearm it in under 10 minutes.

MiG-29 Fulcrum.fun_fact: The MiG-29 has auxiliary air inlets above its wing roots that open on the ground to prevent FOD ingestion, allowing safe operation from rough, unprepared airstrips.

MiG-31 Foxhound.role: Long-range high-altitude interception and airspace denial
MiG-31 Foxhound.fun_fact: The MiG-31 is one of the few fighters capable of sustained Mach 2.83 flight and is used as the launch platform for Russia's Kinzhal hypersonic missile.

Mirage 2000.role: Air superiority, ground attack, and nuclear strike
Mirage 2000.fun_fact: The Mirage 2000 revived Dassault's tailless delta wing layout from the Mirage III era, this time tamed by fly-by-wire technology that turned instability into agility.

Panavia Tornado.role: Low-level supersonic interdiction and ground attack
Panavia Tornado.fun_fact: The Panavia Tornado was one of the first operational aircraft fitted with terrain-following radar, enabling it to automatically fly nap-of-the-earth profiles at high speed and night.

Su-24 Fencer.role: All-weather supersonic interdiction and ground attack
Su-24 Fencer.fun_fact: The Su-24's variable-sweep wings allow it to penetrate enemy territory at very low altitude, using terrain to mask its approach from radar and air defences.

Su-25 Frogfoot.role: Close air support and counter-insurgency ground attack
Su-25 Frogfoot.fun_fact: The Su-25's cockpit is encased in a welded titanium armoured tub capable of withstanding 23mm cannon rounds — a design philosophy it shares with the American A-10.

Su-34 Fullback.role: Supersonic precision strike and air superiority
Su-34 Fullback.fun_fact: The Su-34 has a unique side-by-side cockpit with a small galley and a fold-out bunk, allowing crew rest during long-range missions — a comfort unique among frontline jets.

Su-57 Felon.role: Stealth air superiority, ground attack, and suppression of enemy air defences
Su-57 Felon.fun_fact: The Su-57 has radar arrays embedded across its entire airframe rather than just in its nose, providing a full 360-degree situational awareness picture without any mechanical antenna movement.

YF-23 Black Widow.fun_fact: The YF-23 reportedly outperformed the YF-22 in speed and stealth, yet lost the ATF competition — some analysts believe Northrop's struggle to demonstrate agility in flight tests was the deciding factor.

AH-64 Apache.role: Anti-armour attack and close air support
AH-64 Apache.fun_fact: The AH-64E's Longbow fire control radar can classify and prioritise up to 128 ground targets simultaneously and cue the crew to engage the most critical six in under 30 seconds.

Akinci UCAV.role: Long-endurance armed reconnaissance and precision strike
Akinci UCAV.fun_fact: The Akinci is Turkey's first UCAV capable of carrying air-launched cruise missiles, including the locally developed SOM-B2 subsonic cruise missile with a range of over 250 km.

CH-47 Chinook.fun_fact: The CH-47 Chinook set an absolute helicopter speed record of 400.87 km/h in 1980, and its tandem rotor design eliminates the tail rotor entirely, channelling all power directly into lift.

CH-53 Stallion.role: Heavy lift assault transport and ship-to-shore logistics
CH-53 Stallion.fun_fact: The CH-53E is the heaviest helicopter in service with any Western military and is powerful enough to lift an entire M198 howitzer complete with its ammunition supply.

DJI Inspire.fun_fact: The Inspire 2 supports a dual-operator mode where one pilot flies the aircraft while a second independently controls the camera, enabling cinema-quality tracking shots impossible with single-operator drones.

DJI Mavic.role: Recreational and professional aerial photography and videography
DJI Mavic.fun_fact: The DJI Mavic 3 folds to the size of a water bottle yet carries a Hasselblad-branded 4/3 CMOS sensor capable of shooting 5.1K cinema-quality video with 12.8 stops of dynamic range.

DJI Phantom.role: Aerial photography, videography, and survey mapping
DJI Phantom.fun_fact: The original DJI Phantom 1, released in 2013, is credited with single-handedly creating the consumer drone market by making aerial photography accessible to non-pilots for the first time.

Ka-52 Alligator.role: Reconnaissance, attack, and target designation for ground forces
Ka-52 Alligator.fun_fact: The Ka-52 uses a coaxial contra-rotating rotor system that completely eliminates the need for a tail rotor, allowing it to rotate freely in any direction and fit into far tighter storage spaces than conventional helicopters.

MQ-9 Reaper.role: Long-endurance armed reconnaissance, surveillance, and precision strike
MQ-9 Reaper.fun_fact: The MQ-9 Reaper can loiter over a target area for up to 27 hours carrying Hellfire missiles and precision bombs — fundamentally changing the nature of persistent strike and surveillance operations.

Mi-24 Hind.role: Anti-armour attack and armed troop assault transport
Mi-24 Hind.fun_fact: The Mi-24 Hind is unique in combining a powerful gunship with a troop-carrying cabin, earning it the nickname 'flying IFV' (infantry fighting vehicle) — it can kill tanks and deliver soldiers in the same mission.

Mi-28 Havoc.role: All-weather anti-armour attack and close air support
Mi-28 Havoc.fun_fact: The Mi-28N features a mast-mounted radar positioned above its rotor head, allowing it to observe and designate targets while the rest of the aircraft remains hidden behind terrain or buildings.

RQ-4 Global Hawk.fun_fact: The RQ-4 can fly non-stop for over 30 hours at 60,000 feet and survey an area the size of Iceland in a single mission using its integrated radar, electro-optical, and infrared sensor suite.

TB-2 Bayraktar.role: Tactical reconnaissance, surveillance, and precision strike
TB-2 Bayraktar.fun_fact: The TB2 Bayraktar became a global symbol of modern drone warfare after its devastating effectiveness against armoured columns in the 2020 Nagorno-Karabakh war and the 2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine.

UH-60 Black Hawk.role: Assault transport, medical evacuation, and combat support
UH-60 Black Hawk.fun_fact: The UH-60 Black Hawk replaced the UH-1 Huey in US Army service and was named after Black Hawk, a war chief of the Sauk nation — a tradition of naming utility helicopters after Native American leaders.
